caption: Figure 1: We empirically investigate the visual appearance of generated images when conditioned on only the text prompt feature or the multimodal feature of target image and the text prompt using Z-Image Turbo with 8 steps.

Figure 2: Method overview. For each training pair, we first pass the prompt alone and the prompt together with the target image through the encoder to obtain c_s and c_t. We then sample a few-step trajectory using the student branch. Teacher and student predict velocities on the same trajectory states, and the student is updated by the D-OPSD loss.
Figure 3: Visual comparison on Z-Image-Turbo under LoRA customization. Vanilla SFT sacrifices few-step quality, PSO overfits, D-OPSD keeps few-step quality while learning the new concept.

Figure 4: Visual comparison under full fine-tuning on the anime domain. SFT / PSO lose few-step quality, D-OPSD adapts to the new domain while preserving the original few-step behavior and prior knowledge.
Figure 5: User study. All images use identical noise. D-OPSD wins on image quality, aesthetics and prompt following against PSO, Vanilla SFT and even the base model.
Figure 7: When the teacher cannot produce concept-consistent samples under multimodal conditioning, no valid supervision signal exists and training fails.
